chapter_title: What is Virginal; or, otherwise, what is Continent

spiritual_reading.full_translation:
The state called pure belongs to the hidden arcana of the highest heaven. It is called pure because it is the whole quality of wisdom that has never been tainted by evil, nor entered into combat with hell.

The state called self-restrained belongs to the arcana of wisdom that did descend into obscurity and was mingled with falsity. In that mingling it was profaned in external forms of life, yet afterward it was raised again into wisdom; therefore it is called self-restrained.

Those who are fully purified, when they stand against hell, do not admit evil into themselves, nor are they overcome by it; they remain untouched by spiritual death.

Self-restraint, however, is wisdom that was mingled with falsity and afterward purified, gathered up out of disordered lower affections, and fixed again in the higher heaven. It is called self-restrained because it first admitted the delight of evil, but afterward was cleansed of that delight and made holy.

Purity is also wisdom purified by a Divine pattern of mediation: it is raised into more interior degrees and confirmed in a formed likeness of heavenly order.

Self-restraint is likewise the remaining portion of that wisdom which, after purification, still lingers in lower things: it rises and descends through successive changes of state. Part of it also comes to be embodied in the outermost human life; and even that, when it is chosen in that outer life, receives faith in deliverance and becomes holy, and so is named self-restrained.

Purity is the Divine Understanding when it comes and takes on the formed qualities of those who are being saved. Self-restraint is the new will and understanding in a person when it is purified from the former self: it is cleansed, casts off the evil conjoined with it, and becomes self-restrained.

Even in the outermost life, purity is a person whose love has never been bound to profaning delights and has not been defiled by their conjunction; but self-restraint is a person who has lived with such delights, and afterward is cleansed from them and renounces them, and by this turning away is made holy.

These are the kinds of purity and self-restraint in many aspects, for purity and self-restraint exist in many forms.

paragraph_translations.translation: The state called pure belongs to the hidden arcana of the highest heaven. It is called pure because it is the whole quality of wisdom that has never been tainted by evil, nor entered into combat with hell.
paragraph_translations.connection: OPENS the teaching by defining purity as untouched wisdom in the highest degree.
paragraph_translations.notes: The phrase about the “mystery of the aeons of greatness” compresses into highest-heaven arcana; the wording implies a technical cosmology that can only be rendered by function.

paragraph_translations.translation: The state called self-restrained belongs to the arcana of wisdom that did descend into obscurity and was mingled with falsity. In that mingling it was profaned in external forms of life, yet afterward it was raised again into wisdom; therefore it is called self-restrained.
paragraph_translations.connection: DEVELOPS by introducing a second state: wisdom recovered after mixture with falsity.
paragraph_translations.notes: The language of being “defiled in bodies” forces a move to external-life profanation; the source’s tone is more mythic than moral, but the function is clear.

paragraph_translations.translation: Those who are fully purified, when they stand against hell, do not admit evil into themselves, nor are they overcome by it; they remain untouched by spiritual death.
paragraph_translations.connection: DEVELOPS by stating the power of the purified state in temptation-combat.
paragraph_translations.notes: The broken line in the source leaves a gap about coming out against the enemy; rendered as standing in spiritual combat.

paragraph_translations.translation: Self-restraint is wisdom that was mingled with falsity and afterward purified, gathered up out of disordered lower affections, and fixed again in the higher heaven. It is called self-restrained because it first admitted the delight of evil, but afterward was cleansed of that delight and made holy.
paragraph_translations.connection: DEVELOPS by explaining why self-restraint is named from prior contact with evil-delight and subsequent cleansing.
paragraph_translations.notes: “From all the creatures” is treated as out of all lower, various affections; the precise cosmological referent is unclear.

paragraph_translations.translation: Purity is wisdom purified by a Divine pattern of mediation: it is raised into more interior degrees and confirmed in a formed likeness of heavenly order.
paragraph_translations.connection: SHIFTS from moral history to purification through a mediating Divine pattern and elevation of degree.
paragraph_translations.notes: “Ambassador” and “image of the gods” are technical mythic terms; their function reads as mediation and confirmation into heavenly form, but the specific identity remains uncertain.

paragraph_translations.translation: Self-restraint is the remaining portion of that wisdom which, after purification, still lingers in lower things: it rises and descends through successive changes of state. Part of it also comes to be embodied in the outermost human life; and even that, when it is chosen in that outer life, receives faith in deliverance and becomes holy, and so is named self-restrained.
paragraph_translations.connection: DEVELOPS by distinguishing a remnant that cycles through lower states and can be made holy even in the outermost life.
paragraph_translations.notes: The transmigration schema is foreign to the rest of the voice; rendered as repeated changes of state. “Human flesh” forced into ‘outermost human life’ language.

paragraph_translations.translation: Purity is the Divine Understanding when it comes and takes on the formed qualities of those who are being saved. Self-restraint is the new will and understanding in a person when it is purified from the former self: it is cleansed, casts off the evil conjoined with it, and becomes self-restrained.
paragraph_translations.connection: DEVELOPS by internalizing the definitions into Divine influx and personal regeneration.
paragraph_translations.notes: “Light Mind” and “new man/old man/Sin” shift register toward anthropological terms; translated by function as Divine Understanding and regenerated mind.

paragraph_translations.translation: Even in the outermost life, purity is a person whose love has never been bound to profaning delights and has not been defiled by their conjunction. In contrast, self-restraint is a person who has lived with such delights, and afterward is cleansed from them and renounces them, and by this turning away is made holy.
paragraph_translations.connection: DEVELOPS by giving the external, moral-life forms of purity and self-restraint.
paragraph_translations.notes: The source uses sexual imagery as its natural plane; translated into conjunction with profaning delights. Some concreteness is inevitably lost because the instruction forbids retaining natural objects.

paragraph_translations.translation: These are the kinds of purity and self-restraint in many aspects, for purity and self-restraint exist in many forms.
paragraph_translations.connection: CLOSES by generalizing the teaching into multiple distinct forms.

spiritual_reading.overall_coherence: Coherent as a single teaching that defines two spiritual states—untouched wisdom and recovered wisdom—then traces their operation in temptation, elevation of degree, remnants in lower states, regeneration in a person, and finally outward life. The main stumble is the cosmological vocabulary (“aeons,” “Ambassador,” “gods,” “transmigration”), which introduces a different mythic framework; translating by function keeps continuity but cannot preserve all specific doctrinal nuance.

findings.diagnosis: Clean correspondential opening: two states are defined by what the Light does (unmixed vs mixed-and-recovered). The spiritual reading does not stumble here except to paraphrase cosmological nouns.
findings.evidence: Text defines ‘virginal’/‘continent’ by functional relation to mixture and death: “all the light that did not taste of death, nor come to the enemy’s war” (¶3) vs “light that came and was mixed with the darkness… went up to the light” (¶4). The reading’s note: “technical cosmology… rendered by function” indicates vocabulary pressure, not narrative break; the story still runs (unmixed Light vs mixed Light).

findings.diagnosis: Genuine difficulty due to damage/fragment: the line is incomplete, so the spiritual reading has to supply a general ‘temptation-combat’ sense. This is not a voice intrusion; it continues the same functional logic (purity unovercome).
findings.evidence: Coptic/English is broken: “should they come out against the en[emy and shall ... not] taste death, nor [be overcome by him]” (¶5). The reading explicitly flags: “broken line… leaves a gap… rendered as standing in spiritual combat.” No sign of an administrative list or seam; just lacuna.

findings.diagnosis: Mostly clean correspondential continuation; one phrase creates minor cosmological opacity but not a textual disruption. The ‘why named continent’ etymology stays functional (tasted lust → cleansed).
findings.evidence: The explanation is by process: “mixed with the darkness, was purif[ie]d… confirmed in the great[ness]… since it tasted of the lust; but afterwards was cleansed” (¶6). The reading stumble is limited: “‘From all the creatures’… precise cosmological referent is unclear.” That is interpretive uncertainty, not a narrative seam.

findings.diagnosis: Mixed voice at a seam: the teaching is still about purification/elevation (substrate), but it is carried by identity-titles (“Ambassador,” “gods”) that do not arise from functional description and shift the register into mythic administration/officialdom. This is an overlaying identification layer rather than an inserted list; removing it would leave the paragraph too thin and may not improve flow.
findings.evidence: “purified by the ima[ge] of the [A]mbassador… confirmed in the image of the gods” (¶7). The spiritual reading notes the stumble: “‘Ambassador’ and ‘image of the gods’ are technical mythic terms… specific identity remains uncertain.” The paragraph teaches by named mediating office (“Ambassador”) and pantheon label (“gods”) more than by function, but it is integrated into the ongoing contrast virginal/continent and not a detachable inventory.
findings.scope: Annotate ¶7 as a mythic-identificatory overlay within an otherwise functional purification/elevation statement (titles: “Ambassador,” “gods”).

findings.diagnosis: Genuine doctrinal/lexical difficulty rather than an insertion: ‘transmigration’ introduces a different explanatory mechanism, but it is not administrative (no jurisdictions/ranks), and it directly continues the ‘remainder of light’ logic from ¶6. The narrative does not clearly improve by excision because the paragraph supplies the needed ‘remainder’ counterpart to ¶7.
findings.evidence: Text: “remainder of this light… goes up and comes down in transmigration… attain the form of human flesh… be chosen… become an holy one” (¶8). Reading flags the stumble: “The transmigration schema is foreign to the rest of the voice.” However, the paragraph is still functional/processual (remaining light cycles; part enters flesh; can become holy). No authority-language or ranked entities appear.

findings.diagnosis: Clean correspondential internalization into anthropology/ethics (new man/old man; virginity/continence). The register shifts, but it is a normal late-step application from cosmic process to personal process; not an administrative intrusion.
findings.evidence: Functional transformation language dominates: “new man… purified from this old man… strips off the Sin” (¶9) and “man… never joined… not been defiled… Afterwards, he cleanses himself… renounces her” (¶10). The reading notes a ‘shift register toward anthropological terms’ (¶9) and ‘sexual imagery’ (¶10), but it still serves the same two-state schema and participates in the story rather than interrupting it.

findings.diagnosis: Clean closure formula; summarizes multiplicity of forms without adding new machinery. No sign of seam-expansion (no fivefold recast, no new taxonomy).
findings.evidence: “I have taught you the categories… in a great many aspects… in many forms” (¶11). The spiritual reading experiences no stumble here; it functions as a conclusion.

textual_criticism.summary: Findings: 7 total. Clean correspondential substrate dominates (¶3-4, ¶6, ¶8-11). One damaged line (¶5) causing forced paraphrase but not insertion. One mixed/seam-like mythic-identificatory overlay (¶7: ‘Ambassador,’ ‘gods’) where the spiritual reading stumbled on technical titles; recommend ANNOTATE that paragraph rather than excise. No clear administrative inventory blocks and no passages whose removal clearly improves narrative flow.

harmonized_paragraphs.text: What is called ‘virginal’ is assigned to the mystery of the aeons of greatness. And they called it ‘virginal’ by the category of all the light that did not [taste] of death, nor come to the enemy’s war.

However, what is called ‘continent’ occurs to the mystery of the light that came and was mixed with the darkness. It was defiled in bodies [in the garments of the flesh] and went up to the light. [They] called [it ‘co]ntinent’.
Furthermore, the holy vir[gin]als [when they stand in their purity] should they come out against the en[emy and shall ... not] taste death, nor [be overcome by him].

⟨p.249⟩ On the other hand, what is called ‘continent’ [is this li]ght that mixed with the darkness, was purif[ie]d, came [up f]rom all the creatures, and was confirmed in the great[ness]. They called it ‘continent’ since it tasted [of the l]ust; but afterwards was cleansed from it and [become an] holy one.
Furthermore, what is called [‘vi]rginal’ is this light that was purified by the ima[ge] of the [A]mbassador. It wen[t up and] attained [the] he[ights. It was] confirmed in the image of the gods.

Again, what is [called] ‘continent’ is the remainder of this light th[at] remained behind, from what was cleansed. It goes up and comes down in transmigration. Al[so], there is a part [of] it that shall come and attain the form of [hum]an [fl]esh. Again, that one too shall be chosen in the flesh, [accept] the hope, and become an holy one. And they name it ‘continent’.

Furthermore, what is named ‘virginal’ is the Light Mind, should he come and assume the images [of] the ele[ct]. However, on the other hand, what is called ‘contin[ent]’ is the new man, should it be purified from this old man. And it is cleansed and strips off the Sin that is compounded with it, and it becomes a continent one.

And also, what is called ‘virgi[n]al’ in the flesh, is a man if he has [ne]ver joined himself to woman, has not been defiled by intercourse. However, [i]n contrast, what is called ‘continent’, is the man who has a wom[a]n in the world. Afterwards, he cleanses himself from her [and] renounces her. And because of this he [turns back from her] and he becomes an holy contin[en]t one.
Behold, I have taught you the categories [of] the v[ir]ginal and the continent in a great many [as]pects. For what is virginal, or otherwise what is [con]tinent, is in many forms.

changes_summary: No changes made. The only targeted issue was Finding 4 (¶7) with an ANNOTATE recommendation; per instructions, annotation does not alter the paragraph text. All other findings recommended none, so the chapter remains unchanged.
